column1: # G4 phase 3: the DERIVED STRUCTURE
# (docs/capability-review/g4-identity-relations.md). An evaluated
# document has, besides its value, a GRAPH: the set of checked links,
# each from one tree position to another.
# The graph is PATH-NATIVE (ADR-014). There is no entity index, because
# there is no second namespace to index -- a node's address IS its path.
# The node a link starts at is DERIVED from where the link sits: strip
# the list indices, and the first real key above the link is the
# relation, its parent the source. A rel()-minted link carries its
# predicate DECLARED, and is cut at that key wherever it sits, which is
# what makes a map-valued relation report the relation rather than the
# inner label.
# Mode `graph`, four columns; `expect` is the whole graph as JSON.
# BOTH runners additionally re-derive it on a fresh engine and require
# the same bytes: determinism is asserted as a PROPERTY here, not
# claimed in prose. It is what makes a byte-comparable golden possible
# at all -- Go map order is random, so edges are sorted by construction
# rather than by luck.
# G4's deliverable is that this exists and is deterministic. What is
# built on it -- impact analysis ("what reaches $.services.auth?"),
# reachability, node slices -- is a traversal, and its exposure as verbs
# and projections belongs to G7. Relation properties (acyclicity,
# inverse consistency) are phase 5's, and consume exactly this edge set.
# Every expectation was obtained by the parity probe (AGENTS.md).

# The edge's far end is the PATH the address resolved to, not the text
# the author wrote: a relative address means a different node from each
# position it is written at, and an edge set whose far ends were
# spellings could not be traversed. The link's own VALUE is still what
# was written -- `gens` in refer.tsv pins that.
